event.summary: Stop callout's broad descendant claim predates the assigned change
event.detail: Reviewed commit: 2c5a1d5a8ebe7c0d0889ac5db40b272d75ae02cb. TLDR: The intermediate screenshot says Stop ends everything the agent started, although some detached jobs can survive. Details: The assigned patch adds terminal-tab closure to the old wording, which already said 'Stop: ends the agent and everything it started.' SPEC.md, Lifecycle operations, lines 2037-2070 describes the limits: 'jobs a user-run tmux moves outside those groups may survive Stop, Restart, Replace, Delete or tab close; this is accepted as the intent of running them under tmux' and 'a detached process that hides or overwrites its environment survives stop and delete there.' This is not a newly introduced independent defect in the assigned change. Commit 53d618e4a033749efc9f9f10adef168643737b99 subsequently corrects this exact callout to say some detached Linux jobs can keep running. Suggested bucket: other (documentation-capture wording); confidence: confirmed by patch and pinned contract, not execution. proposed_drop: the overbroad claim was pre-existing, and the assigned later patch corrects it; no new regression established. Could-be-highest: no established security or loss-of-work route in these screenshot changes. possible_cover: none searched. Caveat: accepted process-containment limitations do not themselves make inaccurate documentation correct; the basis for dropping is the unchanged pre-existing claim, not specification acceptance of misleading wording.

event.summary: Broad Stop prose is pre-existing; later repair does not erase intermediate wording
event.detail: Reviewed commit: 2c5a1d5a8ebe7c0d0889ac5db40b272d75ae02cb. Exact chronology checked in source: the parent revision already has the row-menu string 'Stop: ends the agent and everything it started. The session and its terminal stay.' at lines 53-56. The reviewed commit changes that string at line 60 to 'Stop: ends the agent and everything it started, and closes its shell tabs. The session and its terminal stay.' It also newly adds a separate header Stop callout at line 26, 'Stop: ends the agent and closes its shell tabs. The session stays.' Commit 53d618e4a033749efc9f9f10adef168643737b99 later replaces only the row-menu explanation at line 61 with 'Stop: ends the agent and closes its terminal tabs. Some detached jobs on Linux can keep running. The session stays.' and adjusts its placement. Contract: SPEC.md at the reviewed revision, Lifecycle operations, describes tab closure and expressly limits descendant cleanup: 'jobs a user-run tmux moves outside those groups may survive Stop, Restart, Replace, Delete or tab close; this is accepted as the intent of running them under tmux'; without a scope, 'a detached process that hides or overwrites its environment survives stop and delete there.' The broad prose is inaccurate at the intermediate revision; a later repair alone would not justify dropping an introduced error. The assigned executable capture test is in review scope, but this particular error is generated prose already present before its patch. Its runnable changes add a header annotation, crop/layout changes and tab-closing wording; neither Stop action is clicked or implemented by this test. No changed runnable capture logic is shown to stop incorrect processes or manufacture the broad behavior claim for the first time. Suggested bucket: other (noncatastrophic capture/documentation error). Confidence: confirmed from parent/reviewed/later source and pinned contract; no capture, rendering or runtime behavior was observed. proposed_drop: no newly introduced defect in the unchanged broad claim; not ordinary-docs exclusion, not acceptance of inaccurate prose, and not merely the later repair. Could-be-highest: no established route from this wording to security or loss of user-owned work; it describes an incomplete cleanup guarantee rather than instructing deletion or credential disclosure. possible_cover: none searched. Caveat: parent has not accepted this proposed drop, and this event leaves the full intermediate error and consequence visible for its independent decision.

event.summary: Grid row queries do not include offscreen overscan rows
event.detail: Reviewed commit: 647f0227b7f5b6c5fe443b2d5f0c4a20de0d5513. TLDR: Considered whether the migrated terminal annotations or hover helper could choose an offscreen history match instead of the visible text. Details: overlay.ts:305-318 and e2e/docs-shots/visual-review.spec.ts:334-348 query .grid-terminal-row elements. Pinned crates/farhelm-ui/assets/grid-terminal.js:631-646 creates exactly model.rows DOM rows, sizes each to cellHeight and the screen to model.rows * cellHeight; it does not create overscan/history rows. Lines 547-580 compute a clamped viewport over history and screen. SPEC_impl.md, The grid client, says 'Rendering is one element per visible row with its runs as spans reused in place'. The query therefore covers the drawn view rather than every historical match. Suggested bucket: other (capture tooling); confidence: confirmed source analysis, not execution. proposed_drop: source refutes the offscreen-overscan premise. Could-be-highest: no, consequence considered is incorrect capture annotation only. possible_cover: none searched. Caveat: character-to-cell assumptions remain limited to suitable plain text, explicitly documented in overlay.ts:294-296 and already present before the migration.

event.summary: Check whether annotation callers can target an exit-clipped grid row
event.detail: Reviewed commit: 647f0227b7f5b6c5fe443b2d5f0c4a20de0d5513. TLDR: The migrated annotations query drawn grid rows, but a drawn row is not necessarily visible after an exited terminal is lifted to make room for its exit line. Details: The earlier c2 source check established no overscan rows, which remains correct. Additional synthesis read of crates/farhelm-ui/assets/grid-terminal.js:880-885 finds negative screen margin and clipPath used by layoutExit; paint():919-932 paints model.rows rows and then applies that exit layout. Suspected consequence: an annotation or hover can select a clipped row and fail or point at hidden content. Checks completed: pinned row-count/layout and paint implementation. Exact missing premise: whether any assigned helper caller runs against an exited terminal whose matching text is in a clipped row; inspect callers and staged session behavior before deciding. Suggested bucket: other, capture tooling only. Confidence: unverified pending readily available caller analysis; not execution. proposed_drop: false while caller premise is open. Could-be-highest: no, no established route beyond capture correctness. possible_cover: none searched. Original considered consequence remains an annotation selecting text outside the visible region; the offscreen-history-overscan mechanism was refuted, but actual exit clipping needs a separate caller check.

event.summary: Assigned annotation callers use live, unclipped grid terminals
event.detail: Reviewed commit: 647f0227b7f5b6c5fe443b2d5f0c4a20de0d5513. TLDR: The changed row query does not establish a broken capture in its actual callers. Details: The original concern was an annotation selecting text outside the visible region. Grid-terminal.js:631-646 creates exactly model.rows DOM rows, not history overscan; paint():912-932 renders lineRow(top + y, shape) into those rows, so their text is the drawn viewport. A narrower issue considered during synthesis is real as a helper limitation: layoutExit():868-885 can shift and clip the first rows after exit, and the query does not inspect that clip. Checked all relevant callers: visual-review.spec.ts:451-512 hovers only the scenario's initial and terminal-review sessions; docs/docs-shots/scenario.json5:30-39 and 73-82 assign those running and idle, respectively, without a then override. The regular work-in-a-session and release file-hover shots use the same open running session. All Director.terminalText callers found are capture.spec.ts:117/127 and first-session.spec.ts:55. The video scenario's migrate session is waiting with then: quiet (docs/readme-video/scenario.json5:40-47), and its transcript pauses at the menu before those annotations. The first-session shot opens the docs scenario's running session. stage.ts:73-75 maps running/idle/waiting to spin/quiet/menu rather than exit. Thus none of these callers supplies the missing exited-terminal premise. Suggested bucket: other, capture tooling only. Confidence: confirmed source and caller analysis, not runtime or visual execution. proposed_drop: no established reachable failure in assigned runnable capture logic; overscan is refuted and exit clipping is outside actual callers. Could-be-highest: no, the suspected consequence is a misplaced annotation or failed capture. possible_cover: none searched. Caveats: the helpers are not general guarantees of clipping-aware visibility; adding exited-terminal callers would require revisiting them. Character-index-to-cell mapping remains the existing documented plain-text assumption. This candidate revision closes the c2 synthesis lead; no premise remains open for its actual callers.

event.summary: Update the terminal target helper's obsolete no-row-DOM rationale
event.detail: Reviewed commit: 647f0227b7f5b6c5fe443b2d5f0c4a20de0d5513. TLDR: A maintainer reading the capture helper is still told that terminal lines have no elements, even though the migrated helper now finds and measures those exact row elements. This is inaccurate maintenance guidance, not an established broken capture. Details: The public Director.terminalText docstring at overlay.ts:442-447 says 'The terminal draws its text without an element per line, so this places an invisible tracking element over it'. The same commit rewrites terminalAnchor():289-293 to explain that the grid draws each visible row as .grid-terminal-row and :310-316 to iterate those actual elements and use their bounding boxes. The painter creates exactly model.rows row elements at crates/farhelm-ui/assets/grid-terminal.js:631-646 and paints the visible rows at :919-922. The authoritative SPEC_impl.md, The grid client, describes rendering as one element per visible row and new terminals mounting the grid directly. Exact attribution checked across the whole range: exclusive base 6e423e30068b62c6cfa276c6d720ee35bb70387a has the same public explanation at overlay.ts:440-445, where terminalAnchor():303-315 reads xterm's buffer and cell size. That explanation was valid for the prior capture stack, whose immediate-parent start-stack.sh:150-165 explicitly creates tmux/xterm terminals with --new-terminals tmux. The reviewed commit removes that selector from both supervisors (reviewed start-stack.sh:197-209) and makes the helper grid-only; it updates the private explanation but leaves the public rationale false. Bounded history over the full pinned range returns this as the only overlay.ts change, so this is an introduced stale explanation, not merely old inaccurate text inherited from before the range. Fix by explaining that the match has no element of its own and the tracking anchor covers the matching substring within a row, using row geometry and the grid's cell width, as the new private docstring already does. Suggested bucket: other, source-documentation correctness only. Confidence: confirmed source, caller and whole-range history analysis; no runtime or visual execution. proposed_drop: false. Could-be-highest: no, there is no security, loss-of-work or runtime failure claim. possible_cover: none known from supplied neighbour records; g092/l1 concerns a distinct asynchronous-write rationale, and no coverage sources were searched. Caveat: the tracking helper can remain useful despite row elements; this finding is about the false reason it gives, not a claim that the helper should be removed or that production rendering is wrong.
